summary: This informational RFC describes the about URI scheme, which browsers and some other applications use to point to internal resources such as settings or application info.

eli5.summary: Typing about: followed by something opens a page inside the browser itself rather than a site.

questions: what is the about uri scheme
subtitle: The about: address that browsers use to reach their own built-in pages, such as about:blank.

tldr.problem: Web browsers and some other applications already used about: addresses for their settings, application information and hidden features, but the scheme was never written down or registered.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the syntax of about: URIs in ABNF, says the part after the colon names a browser-specific resource, registers the scheme as Permanent, and creates an IANA registry of well-known tokens with blank as the first entry.
tldr.outcome: about: URIs are mostly specific to each browser, and only behavior shared by two or more browsers is meant to be registered. The RFC is Informational.

today: RFC 6694 is an Informational RFC from August 2012 and, according to the unit metadata, is not obsoleted or updated. It remains the written definition of the about URI scheme.

sections.title: What the about Scheme Is For
sections.content:
RFC 6694 describes the about Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) scheme. Web browsers use it to point to their own internal resources, such as settings, application information and so-called Easter eggs, meaning a hidden feature or joke in an application.

The scheme was already widely used when the RFC was written. The document records it and registers it, so that it has a proper definition.
sections.eli5: Browsers have secret doors to their own settings and surprises. This memo writes down how those doors are named.

sections.title: Syntax of an about URI
sections.content:
An about URI is written with ABNF as the literal about:, followed by an about-token, then an optional about-query (introduced by a question mark) and an optional about-fragment (introduced by a number sign). The token is zero or more pchar characters, and the query and fragment rules come from RFC 3986, Appendix A.

Encoding follows the rules of RFC 3986.
sections.eli5: An about address is the word about, a colon, then a name, and sometimes a question or a bookmark at the end.

sections.title: Meaning and Well-Known Tokens
sections.content:
The about-token names the resource. It is not a hierarchical naming authority. The query part gives extra information about handling or about what the resource should return.

The RFC says no binding can be specified between all possible tokens and their meanings, so the resource is generally considered specific to a Web browser implementation. Some tokens are well-known because their behavior is common. It is recommended that such URIs be handled as the specification listed in the registry says.

This document defines one well-known token, blank. The URI about:blank refers to a blank page in the browser.
sections.eli5: Most of the names only mean something inside one browser. The one name every browser agrees on is blank, which shows an empty page.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Most of the URI security provisions in RFC 3986 do not apply, because they are mainly scoped to schemes used in the Internet.

The RFC warns that about URIs can sometimes refer to sensitive information, such as user passwords stored in a cache, or parameters that, if changed, could affect a user's data. The application therefore needs to ensure that the user's data is secured and that about URIs impose no threats.
sections.eli5: Some of the browser's private rooms hold things like saved passwords, so the browser must keep those doors safely locked.

sections.title: Registrations with IANA
sections.content:
The about scheme is registered in the Permanent URI Schemes registry. The registration names the IETF Applications Area Directors as contact and the IESG as change controller, and says the scheme is predominantly used by Web browsers.

The RFC also creates the about URI Tokens registry with three fields: Token, Description and Reference. The policy is First Come First Served. A registrant gives the token, its intended usage, a contact and a stable specification. As a rule of thumb, behavior common to two or more Web browser implementations can be considered well-known. The initial entry is blank.
sections.eli5: There is now an official list of the shared names. Anyone can add a name if at least two browsers already treat it the same way.

data.title: about URI syntax
data.code:
about-uri = "about:" about-token [ about-query ] [ about-fragment ]
about-token = *pchar
about-query = "?" query
about-fragment = "#" fragment
